proposals.evidence: Prakrit *tēla/tella/tilla*, Hindi *tel* and Gujarati/Marathi *tel* continue *taila* ‘oil’. Prakrit tilla also supplies a comparator for Malvi tīl without assigning the sesame-seed noun *tila*. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10702 gives Prakrit rattī/rāī, Hindi rāt/rātī, Old Marwari rāti and Gujarati/Marathi rāt. Loss of the cluster and final-vowel variation match these regional comparanda. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2462.2 specifically assigns the retained-k one-numerals (Hindi/Nepali/Bengali ek, Punjabi ikk) to *ēkka, while acknowledging that the Middle Indo-Aryan geminate may be emphatic or a learned replacement. The link stops at this section, not a claim about how *ēkka itself originated. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6984 nava ‘nine’ compares Hindi/Awadhi nau, Old Marwari nova and Gujarati/Marathi nav. This is the numeral entry, distinct from nava ‘new’. Contracted and v-bearing variants belong to the same family. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6141 derives regional de- from Middle Indo-Aryan dēti/dēi, remodeled with imperative dēhi and the ‘take’ paradigm. The bare imperative belongs here; diyā and doubled de-de are excluded from this proposal. The local form was checked against the Dardic comparanda in the full CDIAL article; no borrowing arrow was applied to this selected comparison.
